text: Moderate rest periods are believed to provide an ideal compromise between metabolic stress and mechanical tension. A hypertrophy-type workout in which people rested 90 seconds between sets showed significantly greater increases in blood lactate concentration and reductions in pH compared to a strength-type workout with 5 minutes of rest between sets (166). With respect to the effect on loading, Medeiros and colleagues (152) found that using 60-second rest intervals required a reduction of 5% to 10% in each successive set to allow for the maintenance of 8RM to 12RM loads in resistance-trained subjects.
